medicaid_program_name: DC Medicaid, run by the DC Department of Health Care Finance (DHCF). Adults who are not eligible for Medicaid with income from 138% to 200% FPL may instead qualify for the Healthy DC Plan, a Basic Health Plan offered by the DC Health Benefit Exchange through DC Health Link.
medicaid_adult_income_limit_note: DHCF Medicaid Income Limits page: effective 1/1/2026 the limit for Parent/Caretaker Relatives and Childless Adults is 138% FPL (133% + 5% disregard), down from 216%/210% + 5% disregard (FAQ: 221% and 215%). The page's table lists $1,800/month for 1 person, $2,432 for 2, $3,065 for 3, $3,697 for 4. These dollar figures equal 138% of the 2025 FPL, and DHCF's Aug 2025 FAQ says they 'will change again 1/1/2026 to align with federal requirements', so the dollar amounts may be out of date; the 138% FPL limit is the reliable fact. 2027 work requirement: DHCF's 'Federal Changes to Medicaid' page says that starting January 1, 2027, most adults ages 19 to 64 without dependent children must do at least 80 hours each month of work, training, volunteering or similar activities to keep Medicaid, and must renew every 6 months instead of once a year. DHCF's Jan 29, 2026 testimony describes this 'expansion' group as childless adults aged 21-64, so the two DHCF sources give different lower ages.
medicaid_quote: Medicaid income limits for Parent/Caretaker Relatives and Childless Adults decreases to 138% of the federal poverty limit (FPL).
medicaid_work_requirement_quote: Starting January 1, 2027 ... Most adults ages 19 to 64 who do not have dependent children must do at least 80 hours each month
state_subsidy_or_reinsurance_note: No District-funded premium subsidy and no Section 1332 reinsurance program found for 2027. CMS's Section 1332 waiver page has no District of Columbia entry, and no premium-subsidy program appears on the DISB or HBX pages reached (dchealthlink.com itself could not be read). The District's own coverage help is the Healthy DC Plan, a Basic Health Plan run through the DC Health Benefit Exchange (DC Health Link), new on 1/1/2026. DHCF MDL 25-02 (Oct 16, 2025) lists eligibility as age 21-64, US citizen or lawfully present, not eligible for Medicaid or employer coverage, and income from 138% to 200% FPL. The Mayor's Nov 6, 2026 newsletter says the plan is for residents with incomes up to two times FPL and includes vision and dental benefits for 2027. This is a coverage program, not a premium subsidy for private plans; the caller should decide whether it belongs in the 'State help' row.
state_subsidy_quote: Healthy DC Plan is for residents whose incomes are up to two times the federal poverty level

copy.medicaid: The District has expanded Medicaid. Since January 1, 2026, the income limit for parents, caretaker relatives and adults without children is 138% of the federal poverty level. Starting January 1, 2027, most adults under 65 without dependent children must meet a work rule to keep Medicaid. They must do at least 80 hours a month of work, training, volunteering or similar activities.
copy.state_help: The District also offers the Healthy DC Plan through DC Health Link. It is for some adults who do not qualify for Medicaid and have incomes up to two times the federal poverty level. Age and other rules apply. For 2027, it includes vision and dental benefits.

notes_unverified: DC Health Link's own site (dchealthlink.com, including /individuals/plans, /faqs and HealthyDCPlan.com, which redirects there) shows a Cloudflare human-verification check (CAPTCHA) and could not be read. Per the rules it was not bypassed. The 2027 open enrollment dates come from three other DC government sources that agree: the DC insurance regulator's 2027 rates page, DISB's Sep 18, 2026 press release and the Mayor's Nov 6, 2026 newsletter. The owner may want to look at dchealthlink.com in a normal browser to confirm.
The deadline to enroll for January 1, 2027 coverage in DC was not found on any reachable DC government page, so oe_jan1_deadline is null. A third-party site says Dec 15; not used.

The DHCF table's Medicaid dollar figures ($1,800/month for one person, etc.) are 138% of the 2025 federal poverty level, and DHCF's own FAQ says they would change on 1/1/2026. No updated 2026 dollar table was found, so the copy uses only the 138% FPL limit.

Two DHCF sources give different ages for the work-requirement group: the public 'Federal Changes to Medicaid' page says ages 19 to 64, while the Jan 29, 2026 testimony says childless adults aged 21-64. The copy follows the public page.
DHCF says more information on the work requirement 'is coming'. Exemptions and how to report were not checked in detail.

The DC Medicaid expansion status comes from KFF (secondary, Nov 6, 2026) and from DHCF's use of the word 'expansion' for the childless adult group. Medicaid.gov's DC state profile could not be read reliably: curl got 403, and WebFetch returned only template text.

The Healthy DC Plan is a District coverage program (a Basic Health Plan), not a premium subsidy for private plans. It is placed in state_help for the caller or owner to accept or drop. Secondary sources report that some immigration statuses lose Healthy DC Plan and Marketplace tax-credit eligibility starting January 2027 under federal law. This was not verified on a primary page and is not used.
No District-funded premium subsidy for 2027 was found. Only the reachable DISB, HBX, DHCF and CMS pages were checked; dchealthlink.com could not be read.

Checker: the Healthy DC Plan eligibility rules (ages 21-64, citizen or lawfully present, no employer coverage) come from MDL 25-02 for 2026. No 2027 version was found on a reachable DC government page; dchealthlink.com is blocked by a Cloudflare check that was not bypassed. Federal H.R. 1 changes for some immigration statuses in 2027 are not checked, so the copy only says 'Age and other rules apply'.
